description:
David Lebovitz vs. Gelato Messina: The Chocolate Sorbet Showdown! 🍫🍨

Which chocolate sorbet reigns supreme? In this video, I pit David Lebovitz’s famous chocolate sorbet recipe against Gelato Messina’s legendary chocolate sorbet to find out which one is the richest, creamiest, and most intensely chocolatey! 🍫🔥

Both recipes are known for their deep cocoa flavor and smooth texture (?), but which one will come out on top? Watch as I compare the ingredients, techniques, and final taste to crown the best homemade chocolate sorbet!

💬 Which chocolate sorbet do you think will win? Have you tried making either of these at home? Drop a comment below!

📌 Timestamps:
00:00 – Intro 🍦
01:07 - Ingredients for both recipes
01:51 – Gelato Messina’s Chocolate Sorbet Recipe Breakdown
04:31 – David Lebovitz’s Chocolate Sorbet Recipe Breakdown
07:52 – Churning & Freezing Process
08:39 -  Scooping and slow mo's
09:10 – Taste Test & Comparison 🍫
10:29 – The Final Verdict! 🏆

🔥 What You’ll Learn in This Video:
✔️ The key ingredients and techniques in each recipe
✔️ How to achieve a smooth, creamy texture without dairy
✔️ A side-by-side taste test comparison
✔️ Which recipe is better for home ice cream makers

✅ SUBSCRIBE for more ice cream and sorbet recipe tests!

comments.text: I had a terrific cocoa sorbet at a place in Mexico City. I spoke with the owner and he said he uses dates in it for body. I tried it at home and it came out great. Worth a try.
comments.author: @chefjohnb1

comments.text: What was the texture like?
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: @PolarIceCreamery very smooth, dense, almost chewy. I think he uses all cocoa. I used about 100g of dates for 1kg of mix cooked with water and a little baking soda then puréed and proceeded similar to the perfect scoop cocoa sorbet with some melted chocolate. I need to make it again with a few tweaks, I think I’ll try 150g of dates.
comments.author: @chefjohnb1

comments.text: I tried thr david version. Mine didnt turn out well.
comments.author: @zelos96

comments.text: David Lebovitz version is pretty good, what went wrong?
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text:
​​ @PolarIceCreamery  for starters. I didnt have an ice cream machine. 

So i did a water ice bath. But the mixture wouldn't thicken. I froze even the bowl. 

So i put it in the fridge. And stir every 30minutes. Up to 3 hours. To break the ice crystals. 

It came out grainy. For some reason. Mahbe because of the chocolate i use. I use ritter sport chocolate 74%. Cocoa.

And i found that the flavour is nice. Just maybe abit too sweet for my liking. 

So the problem maybe because of the chocolate i use , and the texture. 

Is there a way to do it by hand? Or do i need an ice cream machine to make this? Also how many grams of sugar can i reduce? 

I do love the bitter flavour of the 70% chocolate.

The final product cane out grainy and like a thick paste. It also melts super fast.
comments.author: @zelos96

comments.text: @zelos96 so you changed his recipe considerably, that’s why it didn’t work. You used a chocolate that has high sugar content, that changes the freezing point. It’s not a “no churn” recipe so that also didn’t help.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text:
​​ @PolarIceCreamery i use a chocolate that has 74% cocoa solid. Its much more bitter compared to your one in the video which is 60% cocoa solid.

So you do need the an ice cream machine to make it work.
comments.author: @zelos96

comments.text: @zelos96  yes but it’s 25% sugar!  Don’t confuse cocoa solids with other ingredients.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text:
​​​​ @PolarIceCreamery  so is there any solution to this problem?

Like do i need to change rhe chocolate that i use?

So this recipe only be able to use 60% cocoa solid? And need an ice cream machine to work is it correct?
comments.author: @zelos96

comments.text: @PolarIceCreamery  It didn't work for me either. I don't have an ice cream machine so I used a tricycle. I also replaced the sugar with gravel. It didn't taste very good before freezing, so I put it under my porch for three days, occasionally pacing back and forth on the porch while thinking about Batbat, a superhero I invented that is half bat and half bat. Even after that, my mixture didn't seem to have frozen at all. If anything, it was even more liquidy than when I'd started and also had grown what appeared to be fur. It seemed to lack chocolate flavor despite replacing the cocoa with the absence of cocoa. I am also pretty sure it growled at me. Any ideas?
comments.author: @jordanonebillion

comments.text: @jordanonebillion   😂 Batbat.... send that idea to studios ASAP👌
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: I am not near my book but doesn’t David say to put the mix into blender for 15 seconds before churning, as a critical step?  Great video.
comments.author: @p1skelly

comments.text: He does but it’s not needed.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: One thought ... when Palumbo specifies 5g stabilizer, he's probably thinking of a commercial blend like Cremodan. This is not the equivalent of 5g pure gums. Because these blends usually include emulsifiers (sorbates, glycerides) as well as someting inert like maltodextrine, to prevent clumping. So I believe that by using taro gum, you effectively used more than he does. I blame him for not mentioning what he uses ... but it seems most pastry chefs leave out that detail.
comments.author: @paulraphael

comments.text: You are right but the video was mostly to make a point about the recipe and the book. The problem is not the amount it’s the fact he wrote a recipe book for commercial (which no one is going to use) AND home use (which the recipes re rubbish for). It’s just a really bad book to be honest. A total waste of time making it.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: I wonder if that Gelato Massina recipe is meant to be frozen at -12 C like a traditional gelato would be. A quick check gives me a PAC of 310 and a serving temp of -11.9 C given a 20% overrun. On the other hand, it doesn't make a lot of sense, very very few people have a freezer at a higher temperature specifically for ice cream and sorbet.
comments.author: @coffeeandshots

comments.text: I think the recipe book is actually just a bad one. It’s been made as a marketing tool as opposed to being “correct” for home makers. It has commercial recipes and directions for home makers but in reality, the recipes do not work for home users very well.

comments.text:
I really liked the video. 
I only gotta say I was expecting for your modification to improve both or your favorite one. 
Chocolate is indeed one of the most difficult flavors to master. Most chocolate flavor Ice creams are always powder based, giving it a flavor profile too different from what we actually know as real chocolate. I know that is to be expected since the cocoa was skimmed, taking most of its fat, but to me, a chocolate lover myself, is a regular frustration when trying this flavor in most ice cream parlors. In other words, the cocoa butter is gold, I really miss it in most chocolate ice creams I had. I know is also difficult to tame the cocoa butter when frozen, since it will be rock hard but that is also when I/we expect you to step in and tell us the magic. :P
I know I'm long winded but basically is a great difference flavorwise when comparing a ice cream and a actual chocolate bar. Its like the ice cream didnt come from actual chocolate.
If you ever modify this recipe to make it better, share it with us.
comments.author: @rodrigoadea
